alt: The USS Gerald R. Ford (CVN-78), the lead Ford-class aircraft carrier, photographed at sea near the Solent off the English coast in 2022 — the class whose EMALS electromagnetic launch system is at the centre of the reversal decision
story: On August 13, 2026, Trump signed a directive ordering Ford-class aircraft carriers to replace EMALS — the electromagnetic launch system the Navy spent $4+ billion extra on because steam was 'outdated' — with steam catapults starting from the USS Doris Miller (CVN-81); the catch is that nobody in the US has built a steam catapult in roughly twenty years, the reversal will cost billions more and could delay the carrier from 2034 to the end of the next decade.
why_funny: The US Navy replaced steam catapults with billion-dollar electromagnetic ones because steam was old-fashioned, then ordered the billion-dollar electromagnetic ones replaced with steam because steam is reliable — making both decisions simultaneously correct and catastrophically expensive.
